subject.size_in_frame: running straight at the lens, growing from about 0.30 to 0.70 of frame height across three seconds

headroom: starts generous at about 0.30 of frame height of sky and grass above her and closes to about 0.08 as she arrives — the frame fills up rather than reframes.
horizon_eyeline: Low wide at 0.9 m from the burrow mouth: the far field line runs level across at 0.30 of frame height, the S01 elm standing up out of it at frame centre, x 0.50. Her eyeline rises through that line as she comes on, crossing it at about the two-second mark.

layers.fg: hawthorn stems arching in from the left and right edges and across the top, making a dark ragged frame-within-the-frame
layers.mg: Alice coming out of the long grass straight toward camera, dead centre
layers.bg: the sunlit field going back, and pinned in the background centre the elm she was lying under a minute ago

gaze.note: she runs at the lens and looks past it at the hedge foot; no lead room is given because there is nowhere left to go — the hedge is behind camera. She does not look back at the elm, and the composition offers her every chance to: it is directly behind her head for the whole shot.

balance: Bilaterally symmetrical and frontal — figure centred, elm centred behind her, hawthorn bracketing both sides. The tidiness is the check in the acceleration: the one still, ordered frame in a scene of streaming grass.
leading_lines: The hawthorn arch closes the top and sides and funnels everything to the centre; the flattened track she makes through the grass runs from the elm straight down the middle of frame to her feet — her whole afternoon in one line.
eye_first: Alice at centre, then past her shoulder to the elm behind her, which is the point of the frame.
constraint_binding: Static — the first check in the acceleration. The elm is held on the exact vertical centre line for all three seconds, so its meaning survives without a push-in or a rack.
